caveats: Requires two threads to call scheduling methods (enter/call_at/call_after/enter_after/call_repeatedly) on the same Timer concurrently before it has started; library usage unconfirmed.
The consequence (second Thread.start raising RuntimeError rather than two live threads) follows CPython stdlib threading semantics outside this tree.

subclaims.reason: ensure_started at celery/utils/timer2.py:110-114 checks `not self.running and not self.is_alive()` then calls self.start() with no lock held, and _do_enter at celery/utils/timer2.py:116-118 calls it before acquiring self.mutex. `running` is set True only inside run() at celery/utils/timer2.py:81 by the timer thread itself, so it cannot guard the window, and is_alive() is False for a never-started thread. Two threads (e.g. the consumer path via celery/worker/strategy.py:119 or celery/worker/consumer/consumer.py:350 and the heartbeat/eventer callback via celery/worker/heartbeat.py:49-54, both sharing the one w.timer from celery/worker/components.py:38) can both pass the check before either calls start(). The window spans many bytecodes including the is_alive() call, so a switch between bytecodes suffices under the GIL. The second start() raises RuntimeError per Thread semantics, so one caller fails.
